hook_text: Ten May 1994. Jets roar over the Union Buildings, and a man who spent twenty-seven years in prison becomes president. What happened next?
clip_script: The Union Buildings in Pretoria, the tenth of May 1994. Leaders from around the world watch as Nelson Mandela takes the oath as South Africa's first democratically elected president. Air force jets fly over trailing the colours of the new flag. His government includes former enemies, in a Government of National Unity. Its tasks are huge: to heal a divided country, build houses, bring water and electricity, and write a new constitution.
visual_style: Whiteboard Union Buildings with crowds on the lawns, jets in the sky, then a cabinet table with three party colours, then houses, taps and power lines appearing.
mood: Joyful and proud, then thoughtful about the hard work ahead.
pacing: A big celebratory opening, then a steady look at who governed and what they did.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write down three things the first democratic government set out to do.
